static check: Found 2 errors without running a simulation.
- error/floating_net [V1, Vin]: Net 'Vin' has only one connection (V1), so no current can flow through it. -> Either connect 'Vin' to the rest of the circuit or remove V1.
- error/floating_pin [R1, NC_01]: R1 has an unconnected pin. LTspice auto-named it 'NC_01', which is how it labels a pin with no wire attached. -> Wire the dangling pin of R1 to the node it belongs to. In the schematic the pin will have no wire touching it.]
why is my circuit not getting any gain

tool_calls.name: read_netlist

turns.text:
{"type":"answer","text":"Your circuit has no gain because the signal never reaches it: R1's left-hand pin is not wired to the source.

What the netlist actually says:

  V1 Vin 0 AC 0.7 3000
  R1 Vout NC_01 10k      <-- NC_01 is a dangling pin, nothing else touches it
  R2 Vout 0 15k
  C1 Vout 0 6.63n
  .ac dec 10 1k 100k

Net 'Vin' has exactly one connection (V1) and net 'NC_01' has exactly one connection (R1). So V1 drives nothing, and the only things attached to Vout are R2 and C1, both going to ground. Vout is a passive shunt network with no source, so V(Vout) = 0 at every frequency - an infinitely deep null (-inf dB), which is what looks like "no gain".

Fix (this is a rewiring, not a value change, so I can't patch it): in the schematic, draw a wire from R1's free pin to the Vin node / V1's positive terminal. The pin with no wire touching it is the one LTspice renamed NC_01. After that the netlist line should read:

  R1 Vin Vout 10k

Two things to be aware of once it is connected:

1. This is a passive RC network - it can never have gain above 1. At DC/low frequency the output is a resistive divider: R2/(R1+R2) = 15k/(10k+15k) = 0.6, i.e. -4.44 dB. With a 0.7 V AC source you get 0.42 V in the passband. If you actually want gain you need an active stage (op-amp); if you want a unity-passband low-pass, delete R2 (or make it much larger than R1).

2. The corner frequency is set by C1 against the parallel combination R1||R2 = 10k*15k/25k = 6.0k, not by R1 alone:
   f_c = 1/(2*pi*6.0k*6.63n) = 1/(2*pi*3.978e-5) = 4.00 kHz
   (R1 alone with C1 would have been 1/(2*pi*10k*6.63n) = 2.40 kHz.) So check 4 kHz against your intended cutoff - if you meant 2.4 kHz, either remove R2 or raise C1 to 1/(2*pi*6.0k*2400) = 11.1 nF.

Also minor: the "3000" in "AC 0.7 3000" is the AC phase in degrees, not a frequency. 3000 deg = 3000 - 8*360 = 120 deg. Harmless for a magnitude plot, but if you didn't intend a phase offset, change V1's value to "AC 0.7"."}
